name: Fold

unions.name: Fold
unions.comment:
A left fold, which takes zero or more values of type `a` as input and
produces output of type `b`.

values.name: all
values.comment: A `Fold` which tests if _all_ of its inputs satisfy some predicate.

values.name: and
values.comment: A `Fold` which tests if _all_ of its inputs were true.

values.name: andMap
values.comment:
Chain a `Fold` producing a function onto a `Fold` producing its argument.
Designed for pipeline style, when [`map2`](#map2)–[`map6`](#map6) aren't enough:

    succeed (\a b c -> ( a, b, c ))
        |> andMap foldA
        |> andMap foldB
        |> andMap foldC
values.type: Fold.Fold a x -> Fold.Fold a (x -> y) -> Fold.Fold a y

values.name: any
values.comment: A `Fold` which tests if _any_ of its inputs satisfy some predicate.

values.name: average
values.comment:
A `Fold` which computes the arithmetic mean as `sum / length`. Returns
`NaN` for the empty list.

Compared to [`mean`](#mean), this commits to a single final division and so
is slightly more accurate on well-scaled inputs — but `sum` can overflow to
`Infinity` when many large values are combined. Prefer [`mean`](#mean) when
you also need a [`variance`](#variance) (the state is shared via `map2`), or
when overflow is a concern, or when you want `Maybe` semantics on empty
input.

    average : Fold Float Float
    average =
        map2 (/) sum length

values.name: distributed
values.comment:
Lift a `Fold` so it consumes a stream of functions `e -> a` and produces a
function `e -> b`. At every point `e`, the resulting function is the value the
original fold would have produced from the stream of `a`s obtained by applying
each input function to `e`.

    foldList [ \e -> e + 1, \e -> e * 2, \e -> e - 3 ] (distributed sum) 10
    --> 30  -- == 11 + 20 + 7
values.type: Fold.Fold a b -> Fold.Fold (e -> a) (e -> b)

values.name: elem
values.comment: A `Fold` which tests if a specific value appeared as an input.

values.name: extend
values.comment:
The comonadic extend operation. Given a function that turns a `Fold` into
an output, produce a `Fold` that emits that output at every step, taking into
account all input seen so far.
values.type: (Fold.Fold a b -> c) -> Fold.Fold a b -> Fold.Fold a c

values.name: foldList
values.comment:
Run a `Fold` on a list of inputs, and then generate a single output. This
is analogous to [`List.foldl`](https://package.elm-lang.org/packages/elm/core/latest/List#foldl).
values.type: List.List a -> Fold.Fold a b -> b

values.name: groupBy
values.comment:
Perform a `Fold` while grouping the data according to a specified group
projection function. Returns the folded result grouped as a `Dict` keyed by
the group.
values.type: (a -> comparable) -> Fold.Fold a r -> Fold.Fold a (Dict.Dict comparable r)

values.name: head
values.comment: A `Fold` which remembers the first input.

values.name: last
values.comment: A `Fold` which keeps the last input.

values.name: length
values.comment: A `Fold` which counts its inputs.

values.name: map
values.comment: Transform the output of a `Fold`.
values.type: (b -> c) -> Fold.Fold a b -> Fold.Fold a c

values.name: map2
values.comment:
Combine the results of two `Fold`s run in parallel over the same input.

    average : Fold Float Float
    average =
        map2 (/) sum length
values.type: (b -> c -> d) -> Fold.Fold a b -> Fold.Fold a c -> Fold.Fold a d

values.name: map3
values.comment: Combine the results of three `Fold`s run in parallel over the same input.
values.type: (b -> c -> d -> e) -> Fold.Fold a b -> Fold.Fold a c -> Fold.Fold a d -> Fold.Fold a e

values.name: map4
values.comment: Combine the results of four `Fold`s run in parallel over the same input.
values.type: (b -> c -> d -> e -> g) -> Fold.Fold a b -> Fold.Fold a c -> Fold.Fold a d -> Fold.Fold a e -> Fold.Fold a g

values.name: map5
values.comment: Combine the results of five `Fold`s run in parallel over the same input.
values.type: (b -> c -> d -> e -> g -> h) -> Fold.Fold a b -> Fold.Fold a c -> Fold.Fold a d -> Fold.Fold a e -> Fold.Fold a g -> Fold.Fold a h

values.name: map6
values.comment: Combine the results of six `Fold`s run in parallel over the same input.
values.type: (b -> c -> d -> e -> g -> h -> i) -> Fold.Fold a b -> Fold.Fold a c -> Fold.Fold a d -> Fold.Fold a e -> Fold.Fold a g -> Fold.Fold a h -> Fold.Fold a i

values.name: maximum
values.comment:
A `Fold` which computes the maximum of its inputs, or `Nothing` if there
were no inputs.

values.name: mean
values.comment:
A `Fold` which computes the arithmetic mean of its inputs via Welford's
online algorithm, or `Nothing` if there were no inputs.

The running mean stays bounded by the data's range (so it never overflows)
and shares state with [`variance`](#variance) and friends when combined via
`map2`. For a one-shot mean of well-scaled data, [`average`](#average) is
simpler and slightly more accurate.

values.name: minimum
values.comment:
A `Fold` which computes the minimum of its inputs, or `Nothing` if there
were no inputs.

values.name: notElem
values.comment: A `Fold` which tests if a specific value did not appear as an input.

values.name: null
values.comment: A `Fold` which tests whether any inputs were seen.

values.name: or
values.comment: A `Fold` which tests if _any_ of its inputs were true.

values.name: prefilter
values.comment:
`prefilter pred f` returns a new `Fold` based on `f` but where inputs will
only be included if they satisfy the predicate `pred`.
values.type: (a -> Basics.Bool) -> Fold.Fold a b -> Fold.Fold a b

values.name: premap
values.comment:
`premap f fold` returns a new `Fold` which applies `f` to each input
before handing it to `fold`. This is the contravariant map on the input side
(compare with [`map`](#map), which transforms the output).

    sumOfSquares : Fold Float Float
    sumOfSquares =
        premap (\x -> x * x) sum
values.type: (a -> b) -> Fold.Fold b r -> Fold.Fold a r

values.name: product
values.comment: A `Fold` which computes the product of its inputs.

values.name: sampleStandardDeviation
values.comment:
A `Fold` which computes the sample standard deviation of its inputs, or
`Nothing` if fewer than two inputs were seen.

values.name: sampleVariance
values.comment:
A `Fold` which computes the sample (Bessel-corrected, `n - 1`) variance of
its inputs, or `Nothing` if fewer than two inputs were seen.

values.name: scanList
values.comment: Run a `Fold` on a list of inputs, generating an output for each input.
values.type: List.List a -> Fold.Fold a b -> List.List b

values.name: standardDeviation
values.comment:
A `Fold` which computes the population standard deviation of its inputs,
or `Nothing` if there were no inputs.

values.name: stepFold
values.comment: Step a fold by providing a single input.
values.type: a -> Fold.Fold a b -> Fold.Fold a b

values.name: succeed
values.comment:
A `Fold` which ignores its input and always produces the given value.

This is useful as the starting point of an [`andMap`](#andMap) pipeline.

values.name: sum
values.comment: A `Fold` which computes the sum of its inputs.

values.name: unfoldFold
values.comment:
Create a `Fold` by providing an initial state, a function which updates
that state, and a function which produces output from a state.
values.type: s -> (a -> s -> s) -> (s -> b) -> Fold.Fold a b

values.name: unfoldFold_
values.comment:
Create a `Fold` by providing an initial state and a function which updates
that state. This is a variant of [`unfoldFold`](#unfoldFold) where the output
is the state itself.
values.type: b -> (a -> b -> b) -> Fold.Fold a b

values.name: variance
values.comment:
A `Fold` which computes the population variance of its inputs, or
`Nothing` if there were no inputs. For a singleton input the variance is `0`.
